newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed unit gets Postal Service pact.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed unit gets Postal Service pact.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp. said Tuesday it received a $55 million contract from the U.S. Postal Service for a system to process handwritten letters.
The computerized system would automate processing mail that would otherwise have to be handled manually.

The contract places Lockheed Martin Federal Systems, the Owego, N.Y.-based subsidiary that received the contract, in a strong position as a supplier and systems integrator in address recognition technology, the company said.

The State University of New York at Buffalo developed the original hand written address interpretation software and will serve as a subcontractor by making the software suitable to be integrated into the U.S. Postal Service's equipment.
Bethesda, Md.-based Lockheed Martin's stock fell 37.5 cents to $92.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
